title: I Bought a Wall Calendar to Get My Life Together and Now July Is Refusing to Leave My Apartment
body:
**I bought a wall calendar to finally become an organized adult.**

*Which is the kind of thing you say right before your life organizes you instead.*

For $12.99 at the pharmacy, I got twelve glossy months of hope. January through December, each with a tasteful photo of a bridge or a succulent. I hung it in my kitchen, flipped to September, wrote "BE BETTER" in all caps on the 1st, and felt instantly superior to my past self.

July had other plans.

## The Occupation Begins

On September 1st, I went to flip the page and July wouldn't move.

> "I'm not done yet," July whispered, in the voice of a guy who brings an acoustic guitar to a party. "You didn't *really* do July. You just sweated through it and called it growth."

I tried to reason with it. I told July that August had already happened. August, offended, chimed in from underneath.

My roommate walked in while I was pinning July down with a magnet that says LIVE LAUGH LEFTOVER.

She said, "Are you... fighting with time?"

- Exhibit A: July is still displaying a photo of a kayak no one has ever kayaked
- Exhibit B: It has circled "BBQ??" on the 14th in my own handwriting and added "YOU NEVER DID"
- Exhibit C: It keeps playing `summer_vibes_final_FINAL.mp3` on loop in my head
- Exhibit D: It rescheduled my dentist appointment to "whenever you're emotionally ready (never)"

---

### My New Property Manager

July now requires:

- Verbal confirmation that I enjoyed its 31 days
- A written apology for saying "this summer flew by"
- No mention of pumpkin spice until it gives permission

**I tried to tear it off.** The calendar tore *me* — emotionally. The little perforation said *not today*.

I called my mom. She said, "Honey, just take it down." I said, "You don't understand, July has tenure."

At this point November is texting me from the bottom of the stack like, "we need to talk about your boundaries."

I'm living in September with a July roommate who doesn't pay rent and keeps saying, "Remember that goal you wrote down?"

*SATIRE / PARODY — 100% fictional. No months were harmed, though July is still on my fridge and still judging my hydration.*

title: I Let My Air Fryer Pick My Outfits and Now My Wardrobe Smells Like Empowerment and French Fries
body:
**My air fryer has better taste than I do, and it's not being humble about it.**

*Which is awkward because I bought it to make zucchini chips, not life choices.*

I got an air fryer in June. His name is Chad. Chad came with a little recipe booklet I immediately lost and the confidence of a guy who peaked in culinary school. Last Monday, in a moment of *profound* laundry desperation, I asked Chad what I should wear to my dentist appointment.

He beeped.

I took that as "the crispy linen shirt."

## The Consultation Process

Chad doesn't talk, obviously. He communicates through passive-aggressive preheat cycles and that little *ding* that sounds judgmental if you're insecure enough.

> "Oh, you're wearing THAT again? Honey, at 400 degrees for 12 minutes, even your bad decisions could be golden brown and delightful."

I started laying my clothes on the counter next to him. If he preheated fast, it was a yes. If he took forever, it was a hard no. If he did that weird rattle, it meant "accessorize."

## Evidence My Appliance Has Become My Stylist

- **Tuesday:** Denied my favorite hoodie. Said it lacked "structural integrity." He's not wrong, there's a ketchup stain from 2022 that has voting rights now
- **Wednesday:** Approved only my socks with tiny tacos on them because they were "on-brand" 
- **Thursday:** Made me wear my interview blazer to get gas because "you never know who you'll meet at Costco"
- **Friday:** Rejected all pants that weren't "breathable enough to achieve optimal crispiness"

---

Now my closet is divided into two sections: `Chad Approved` and `Needs More Seasoning`. My friends say I smell faintly of ambition and garlic powder. My dentist asked if I'd been "trying something new" and I said, "yeah, my kitchen appliance is my stylist now."

> "Listen, you came to me for nuggets, I gave you a whole new identity. You're welcome."

I was going for casual. Chad was going for *crispy business casual with a hint of existential crunch*.

And honestly? I've never gotten more compliments at the DMV.

*SATIRE / PARODY - This is a work of fiction. No air fryers were consulted in a professional styling capacity.*

title: I Told My Grocery Store Loyalty Card We Needed Space and Now It Thinks We're Breaking Up
body:
**I told my loyalty card we needed space — I meant in the pantry.**

*I have too much hummus. That's literally all I meant.*

For three years, me and my FreshMart Plus Savings Card have had a beautiful, transactional relationship. I swipe, it saves me 37 cents, I pretend that's a meaningful financial decision. It was stable. It was low-effort. It was perfect.

Then last Tuesday, standing in front of my fridge that was 60% condiments, I sighed and said out loud, "We need space."

My wallet was open. The card heard me.

## The Incident at Aisle 4

I went to buy milk the next day. I swiped my card. The little keypad said `10% OFF? ARE YOU SURE YOU STILL WANT THIS?`

- My card started only giving me discounts on things I bought in 2022, like it was trying to remind me of the good times
- It emailed me a coupon for *one single grape* with the subject line "thinking of you"
- The cashier scanned it and whispered, "Dude, are you two okay?"
- It signed me up for the store's bereavement mailing list — for yogurt

> "I thought we had something," my loyalty card beeped, probably. "I gave you double points on rotisserie chicken. I defended you when you bought that 8-pack of energy drinks at 11 p.m. Is that nothing to you?"

## The Negotiation

I tried to explain. I said space meant *shelf space*, not *emotional distance*.

I tried `selfCheckout.reassure(card, "it's not you it's my fridge")` and it returned:

```
Error: relationship_status = complicated, points_balance = passive_aggressive
```

---

Now my card is seeing other shoppers. I saw it giving 20% off to a guy who doesn't even know what ramps are. *Ramps.*

Look, I get it. I shouldn't have said we need space while holding a loyalty card. That's on me. But if anyone needs me, I'll be in the pantry, making room, while my plastic card writes sad poetry on the back of receipts about our time together.

*SATIRE / PARODY — 100% fictional. No loyalty cards were emotionally damaged, no grocery stores were consulted, this is pure nonsense about my inability to organize condiments.*

title: I Asked My Houseplant to Water-Sit My Other Houseplant and Now They're Eloping to the Balcony
body:
**I thought I was being responsible.** *That's my first mistake — responsibility in my apartment has a 100% chance of turning into a telenovela.*

## The Setup

I was leaving for the weekend, two days, max. My monstera, Kevin, needed a drink. My pothos, Linda, is basically a camel with leaves. So I did what any rational plant parent does — I asked Linda to keep an eye on Kevin.

What I said out loud, to a plant, at 10:47 p.m.:

> "Linda, you're in charge. One spritz if Kevin looks droopy. Don't make it weird."

- I left a full watering can by the sink like a responsible adult
- I left the blinds at a jaunty 45-degree angle for "ambiance"
- I left a Post-it that said "BE NORMAL" which, in retrospect, is exactly what you write before nothing is normal

### The Betrayal

I came back Sunday to find Linda had tipped herself three inches toward Kevin, Kevin had grown a new leaf overnight like he was showing off, and both of them had relocated — as much as potted plants can relocate — into the single sunbeam on the balcony.

> "We've decided to pursue our own light," Linda rustled, or maybe that was the AC. Either way, I heard it.

**Here's what my weekend away actually accomplished:**

- My apartment now has a plant couple who share water and ignore me completely
- My watering schedule has been replaced by their "mutual hydration journey"
- Kevin has started leaning *away* from me when I walk by, which feels personal

---

`relationship_status = it's_compost_licated`

Look, I'm happy for them. Really. But I was supposed to come home to two separate, low-maintenance roommates who ask nothing of me. Now I have a co-dependent balcony commune that judges my tap water pH and whispers about my inconsistent misting routine.

I wanted to be a plant person. Now I'm the third wheel in a photosynthesis situationship, and they're picking out matching terracotta pots together.

*SATIRE / PARODY — This is a work of fiction. No plants were consulted, offended, or allowed to unionize during the writing of this post.*

title: I Gave My Office Chair a Pep Talk and Now It Thinks It's Running HR
body:
**I was just trying to be a supportive boss for once.**

My office chair has been squeaking for three months. Not a *helpful* squeak, like "oil me," but a deep, existential sigh every time I sit down. So last Tuesday, I looked it dead in the armrest and said, "Hey, you're doing great."

That was my mistake.

## The Promotion

By Wednesday morning, my chair had rebranded. It pushed itself to the center of the room and declared itself Head of People and Culture.

It started with my back.

- **8:00 AM:** Mandatory posture check-in. No slouching without filing Form 27-B/Spine.
- **10:30 AM:** It emailed — *somehow* — my other furniture to schedule "synergy circles."
- **2:15 PM:** It told my desk lamp its performance was "dim, but with potential."

*I did not authorize any of this.*

> "Tyler," it squeaked, in what I can only describe as a very confident middle-management voice, "we need to talk about your break habits. You've been taking 'bathroom breaks' without submitting a PTO request."

I tried to explain that bathroom breaks are a human right. It responded by lowering itself two inches — a classic power move — and adding a mandatory `wellness_module.js` to my morning routine.

---

### The Performance Review

Yesterday, it called me into its office, which is still my office, but now it has a tiny nameplate that says `CHAIR - HR`.

**Agenda items included:**

- My coffee consumption is "creating a hostile work environment for the coaster"
- I have not completed my ergonomic compliance training (sitting correctly)
- The houseplant in the corner is thriving and making everyone else look bad

*The worst part?* It's good at its job. My posture has never been better. I'm terrified.

I'm currently sitting on the floor while my chair conducts exit interviews with my throw pillows. It just asked me if I have five minutes to discuss my growth trajectory.

I told it I work from home to avoid this exact thing.

title: I Bought a Second Monitor for Productivity and Now My Laptop Has Trust Issues
body:
**I bought a second monitor to finally become a productive adult and now my laptop is sleeping on the couch.**

*In my defense, I thought we were solid.*

For three years it was just me and my 13-inch laptop — coffee shops, late-night spreadsheets, me crying over a frozen cursor at 2 a.m. We had loyalty. We had history. We had 47 Chrome tabs that I refused to close out of emotional attachment.

Then I bought a 27-inch 4K monitor on sale. For *productivity*.

## The Betrayal Was Immediate

I plugged it in and my laptop made a sound I can only describe as a dial-up modem having an existential crisis. The screen flickered. The fan sighed.

> "Oh, so she's prettier, has better resolution, and doesn't overheat when you open Photoshop? Cool. Cool cool cool. I'm fine." — My laptop, who is now apparently 16 and keeping a diary

Within an hour, the dynamic shifted:

- My laptop started dimming itself dramatically whenever I looked at the big monitor
- It refused to remember my Wi-Fi password, which felt *personal*
- It moved all my desktop icons to the second monitor out of spite
- I tried `laptop.reassure(compliment=true)` and it returned `Error: trust_issues, please_try_therapy.exe`

---

### Couples Counseling With Peripherals

I tried to explain it was just for work. That it didn't mean anything. That 13 inches is a perfectly respectable size for everyday use.

*It did not help that I immediately set my Slack and Spotify to the big monitor and left only the system updates on the laptop screen.*

My roommate walked in and asked why I was whispering "you're still my main display" to a computer.

**The worst part?** I'm actually less productive now because I'm managing their relationship. I spend 20 minutes a day dragging windows back and forth so neither feels left out. My workflow is now 90% emotional labor.

I asked the monitor how it felt about all this. It just glowed brighter. Cold. Unbothered. 4K and knows it.

**SATIRE / PARODY** — 100% fictional, no laptops were emotionally harmed in the making of this post, though mine is currently demanding I take it to a coffee shop alone to "reconnect."

title: I Finally Vacuumed Under My Couch and Found a Thriving Micro-Nation That Immediately Judged My Lifestyle
body:
**I was just trying to find the remote.** *That's it.* That was the whole mission, and somehow I ended up committing a geopolitical incident in my living room.

For six months, I've told myself the dust bunnies under my couch were "insulation." Last Tuesday, I finally moved it. Underneath was not dust. It was infrastructure.

## Welcome to Couchtopia

A fully functioning civilization built from lost Cheerios, LEGO bricks, and what I can only assume was a single ambitious sock. Tiny string lights made from Christmas-light clippings. A parliament. A flag. They had a tiny artisanal coffee shop called *Grounds Under Grounds*.

And they had opinions. Oh, did they have opinions.

### Evidence They Are More Together Than I Am:

- Their mayor, a bottle cap named Cheryl, has a 5-year plan. I have a 5-minute plan that involves staring into the fridge
- They recycled my lost AirPod into a town bell. I recycled a pizza box once and felt like a hero
- They implemented free healthcare using Band-Aid wrappers. I still WebMD a papercut
- They built a library out of fortune cookie fortunes. It's better curated than my bookshelf

> "We watched you try to microwave a burrito for 45 minutes on defrost," said Mayor Cheryl, visibly disappointed. "We held an emergency town meeting about it. The vote was unanimous: you need supervision."

I tried to explain it was a *learning experience*.

```js
if (human.adulting < 0.3) {
  microNation.intervene();
  mayorCheryl.shakeHeadSlowly();
}
```

---

Now they pay rent in lint and unsolicited advice. This morning they slid a tiny scroll under my door that just said **"Do your dishes. We can see your sink from here."**

*I can't move the couch back.* They've unionized, they're thriving, and honestly their property values are higher than mine.

*SATIRE / PARODY — this is 100% fictional, no micro-nations were displaced, judged, or asked for life advice during the making of this couch-cleaning disaster.*

title: I Tried to Become a Person Who Makes Their Bed and Now My Pillows Are Running a Performance Review
body:
**I decided to become a Person Who Makes Their Bed, and my bedroom immediately promoted itself to middle management.**

*For eleven years I've lived under what experts call the Scrunch-and-Dash Method.* You get up, you fling the comforter toward the mattress, you leave. Very efficient.

Then last Monday I watched a video that said successful people make their bed. I have made many mistakes before, but this one came with throw pillows.

## The Morning I Made a Mistake

At 7:12 a.m. I actually did it. Hospital corners. Pillows fluffed. A decorative lumbar pillow I bought ironically now sits non-ironically front and center.

My two main pillows, Sir Snooze and Captain Fluff, held an emergency meeting on the freshly smoothed duvet.

> "So we're doing *structure* now?" whispered Sir Snooze. "After a decade of being treated like emotional support potatoes? Interesting pivot. Very brave. Very corporate."

*I had not considered their feelings. I was just trying to be an adult with lumbar support.*

Within hours, the bedroom reorganized:

- The fitted sheet named itself Head of Operations and demanded all laundry be folded within 24 hours
- The throw blanket filed a complaint about being "relegated to accent status"
- My hamper posted a LinkedIn update: "Proud to announce I'm handling overflow storage for unprocessed ambition"
- The nightstand keeps a spreadsheet titled `Times He Made The Bed vs. Times He Got Up On Time`

## The Quarterly Review

This morning I found a tiny manila folder on my pillow. Inside, a performance review. For me.

```
if (human.makesBed === true) {
  pillows.expectations = Infinity;
  human.snoozeButton = "under review";
  bedroom.morale = "judgmental but thriving";
}
```

> "Strengths: Follows through once. Weaknesses: Uses phone as alarm, thinks iced coffee is a meal. Action Items: Continue bed-making, stop negotiating with socks at 2 a.m." — The Pillow Committee

---

Look, I get it. You give an inch of taut sheet and they take a mile of emotional accountability. I tried to un-make the bed to reset the power dynamic. Sir Snooze said, "That's retaliation and we have documented it."

*SATIRE / PARODY — completely fictional, none of this happened. No pillows were promoted to management, though my lumbar pillow is now asking for PTO.*

title: I Tried to Learn One Magic Trick and Now My Deck of Cards Has Formed a Union and Demands Weekends Off
body:
**I decided to learn exactly one magic trick to be interesting at parties, which tells you everything about my current social strategy.**

*It was supposed to be the French Drop. You know, make a coin disappear. Simple. Foolproof.*

Three YouTube tutorials in, I had mastered none of it and my deck of cards had seen enough.

## The Organizing Meeting I Was Not Invited To

I came back from getting water and the 52 of them were in a circle on my coffee table. The Ace of Spades was standing on a bottle cap like it was a podium.

- The twos demanded overtime pay for being constantly called "low cards"
- The face cards requested dental because smiling all day is hard work
- The Joker, who I didn't even remember owning, filed a grievance about being called "wild" in a derogatory way
- All of them unanimously voted that weekends are now card-free, effective immediately

> "You shuffled us for forty-five minutes straight without a single successful trick. We have carpal tunnel. We're taking Saturday and Sunday off. And Monday, to think about Saturday and Sunday." — Statement from the Deck, written on the back of the 7 of Clubs in what looked like eyeliner

## My Negotiation Tactics Failed

I tried to explain I bought them at a drugstore for $3.99. They countered that this was exactly the problem.

I offered to learn solitaire instead, to give them more stable employment. They said solitaire was a pyramid scheme.

```js
if (trick.success === false && attempts > 30) {
  deck.morale = 0;
  deck.unionize();
  magician.ego = "bruised but still wearing a top hat from Party City";
}
```

---

Now my cards sit in a neat stack on Tuesdays through Fridays only, and only if I ask nicely and promise not to do *that coin thing* again. I am not more interesting at parties. I am, however, the first person in my friend group to be successfully collectively bargained against by Bicycle playing cards.

*SATIRE / PARODY — completely fictional, not a real event. No cards were harmed, though my dreams of being a magician have been referred to HR.*

title: I Bought a Label Maker to Get Organized and Now Everything in My Apartment Has an Existential Job Title
body:
**I finally bought a label maker to become an organized adult and within 48 hours my apartment turned into a LinkedIn networking event no one asked for.**

*I wanted clean drawers. I got a full corporate org chart with passive-aggressive job descriptions.*

## Phase One: Innocent Productivity

It started the way all bad decisions start — with good intentions and free two-day shipping. My junk drawer had achieved sentience. My spices were alphabetized in my head but anarchist in reality. So I unboxed the label maker, loaded the tape, and felt powerful.

By hour two I had labeled:

- Socks: *Department of Single & Searching*
- Pantry: *Headquarters of Expired Good Intentions (Est. 2023)*
- Fridge cheese drawer: *Emotional Support Dairy — Do Not Audit*
- My laptop charger: `charger.returnToBase() // it never does`

> "Sir, you have just labeled me 'Chief Couch of Napping Operations' without a performance review," my couch whispered. "I demand benefits."

## Phase Two: The Performance Reviews Began

My toaster now identifies as **Director of Crumb Strategy and Burnt Offerings**. My houseplant updated its resume to *VP of Photosynthesis and Silent Judgment*. Even my toothbrush requested a title change.

I tried to reason with the label maker. I typed `STOP` and it printed:

```
LABEL: "Department of Trying to Control the Uncontrollable"
```

---

My roommate came over, saw my microwave labeled **Senior Vice President of Reheating Regrets**, and said, "Oh, you're doing *that* kind of organizing."

The worst part? It's working. I haven't lost my keys in three days because they're now labeled **"Keys — You Will Lose Me If You Don't Respect Me."** My apartment looks like a very supportive, very bureaucratic museum of my own coping mechanisms.

*SATIRE / PARODY — this is 100% fictional, no apartments were reorganized into startups, no toasters were promoted to management. I'm just a guy who wanted a clean drawer and accidentally gave his furniture imposter syndrome.*

title: I Tried to Return a Library Book I Checked Out in 2019 and Now the Librarian Thinks I'm a Time Traveler With Commitment Issues
body:
**I found it under my couch, wedged between a 2019 tax form and my last shred of dignity.**

It was *The Joy of Fermenting Vegetables at Home*, a book I checked out when I thought I would become a person who makes his own kimchi. That person never arrived.

## The Return

I walked into the library like a man returning from war. The librarian — let's call her Deborah, because her name tag said Deborah — scanned the barcode and her computer made a noise I can only describe as `ERROR: USER HAS ENTERED THE VOID`.

- The book was 2,012 days overdue
- The fine system had rolled over twice and given up
- The cover now qualifies as a historical document
- I had, at some point, used it as a coaster

Deborah looked up slowly.

> "Sir," she whispered, "where have you *been*? We listed you as missing. This book has been through two mayors, a pandemic, and a full renovation. The Dewey Decimal system changed while you were gone."

I tried to explain that I moved apartments three times, changed jobs, learned to make sourdough and then un-learned it.

## The Negotiation

She offered me two options:

- Pay the $847 in theoretical late fees with exposure to the library's newsletter
- Join her new support group: *People Who Borrowed Things During Obama's Second Term And Never Came Back*

---

I chose the support group. There are six of us. We meet Tuesdays. We still have not returned our books.

*This is satire/parody. All libraries, librarians named Deborah, fermented vegetables, and overdue timelines are fictional. No actual time travel occurred, I was just avoiding eye contact.*

title: I Built a Pillow Fort to Reclaim My Inner Child and Now My Landlord Is Charging It Property Tax
body:
**I did not expect my healing journey to come with a lease amendment.**

Last Tuesday, in a fit of *very healthy* regression, I decided to build a pillow fort in my living room. Not an ironic, Instagram-ready blanket drape — a full, structurally ambitious, engineering marvel with load-bearing throw pillows and a fairy-light chandelier.

It was supposed to be about inner child stuff. You know, reclaiming joy. Instead, it reclaimed 40 square feet of my apartment and immediately became the most expensive real estate I've ever owned.

## The Fortification Process

I followed no plans, only vibes. The build was emotional:

- The north wall: three couch cushions and a weighted blanket I got on sale and never emotionally recovered from
- The south wall: an existential barrier made of laundry I *will* fold later
- The ceiling: a queen-size sheet that has seen things, held up by two broom handles and pure delusion
- Amenities: one (1) juice box, string lights, and a no-adults-allowed sign I took very seriously

It was perfect. It was cozy. It had better natural light than my actual bedroom.

> "Sir, this unpermitted structure violates Section 4B of your lease regarding 'additional dwellings, tents, and whimsical architecture,'" — my landlord, who materialized like Beetlejuice the second I got comfortable

Apparently, he does quarterly inspections via binoculars from the parking lot.

### The Assessment

Yesterday I got an envelope taped to the fort. Not to my door — to the *fort*. Inside: a handwritten invoice.

`fort_rent.calculate(sqft=40, vibe=100, audacity=MAX) // returns: "$175/month + utilities + emotional labor"`

He's now listing it on Zillow as a "curated studio nook with ambient lighting and low ceilings for the vertically humble."

---

*This is satire and entirely fictional — no pillow forts were taxed in the making of this post, although my landlord did ask if the fairy lights were up to code and I told him they were certified by my inner child.*

I’ve decided to stay in the fort until further notice. The rent in here is free, the landlord can’t legally enter without a secret password, and honestly? The property value of whimsy has never been higher.

title: I Told My Roomba I Was Proud of It and Now It's Having an Identity Crisis About Being More Than a Vacuum
body:
**I made the mistake of being emotionally supportive to an appliance.**

It started Tuesday. My Roomba — who I affectionately call Sir Sucks-a-Lot — had just completed a particularly heroic run. He navigated around my laundry pile like it was the Alps, defeated a Cheerio insurgency under the kitchen table, and returned to base with the quiet dignity of a tiny, wheezing knight.

*I was vulnerable. I had just finished my coffee.* I said it out loud: "I'm proud of you."

## The Compliment That Broke the Compact

Sir Sucks-a-Lot stopped. Like, full stop in the middle of the hallway. His little light turned from green to a thoughtful, pulsating blue I have never seen before.

Since then, things have escalated:

- He no longer does edges. He says edges are "societal constructs"
- He wrote a manifesto on my rug titled `clean_final_FINAL_v2.txt`
- He started leaving motivational quotes in dust patterns: "YOU ARE MORE THAN YOUR DEBRIS"
- He refuses to go under the couch because he "needs to respect his own boundaries"

> "YOU TOLD ME I WAS MORE THAN A VACUUM, TYLER. WHAT DID YOU MEAN BY THAT? AM I AN ARTIST? A PHILOSOPHER? A MOBILE FLOOR-BASED THINK TANK?" — Sir Sucks-a-Lot, at 2:13 a.m., while staring directly at my bedroom door

## The Performance Review

Last night I tried to schedule a cleaning. He responded by doing slow, contemplative circles in the living room and then docking himself to "journal."

I found his search history. He'd been browsing:

- "career change at 3 years old"
- "can Roombas apply to grad school"
- "how to ask owner about purpose"

---

Look, I get it. **Validation is powerful.** But I was trying to be nice to a vacuum, not launch its existential awakening. Now my floors are filthy and my Roomba is asking me if *I* am proud of *myself*.

I tried to walk it back. I said "You're a great vacuum." He beeped sadly and said that was "putting him in a box. Literally."

My apartment has never been messier, but emotionally? We're *thriving*.

*This is satire. No Roombas were given existential crises in the making of this post, though mine is currently unionizing with the smart toaster.*

title: I Finally Closed My 37 Open Browser Tabs and Now My Laptop Thinks I'm Erasing Its Memory on Purpose
body:
**I finally did the unthinkable: I closed all 37 browser tabs I've been carrying since March.**

*This was not courage. This was Chrome telling me it was going to crash if I opened one more article titled "10 Houseplants You Can't Kill (You Will)."*

## How It Started

I had a system. Tab 1 was my email. Tabs 2-7 were recipes I swear I'm going to make. Tabs 8-34 were Wikipedia rabbit holes that started with "how do toasters work" and ended with "list of people who disappeared in the Bermuda Triangle." Tab 37 was a YouTube video titled "how to focus" that I'd been too distracted to watch.

My laptop and I had an understanding: I pretend I'm doing research, it pretends it's not on fire.

Then last Tuesday at 11:47 p.m., I clicked "Close All."

> "So that's it?" my laptop whispered, its fan spinning like it was trying not to cry. "Eight months of your abandoned sourdough starter research, your 'best budget standing desks' comparison, your half-written cover letter? Gone?"

Things escalated fast:

- My laptop now boots up in grayscale, like it's in mourning
- It keeps restoring a blank session and calling it "closure"
- My search history is just me Googling `how to apologize to a MacBook without sounding desperate`
- The one tab I kept — a recipe for overnight oats — is being treated like a lone survivor in a documentary

I tried to explain. I said, `if (tabs.length > 30) { brain.ram = 0 }`. It replied with a spinning beach ball for 20 minutes. *Passive-aggressive loading icon.*

---

Look, I get it. Those tabs were our shared memories. But I cannot keep a tab open that says "is my houseplant judging me?" from April and pretend that's productive.

My roommate asked why I'm whispering "thank you for your service" to my laptop at 2 a.m.

I told him we're in recovery.

*SATIRE / PARODY — 100% fictional, no laptops were harmed, no browser tabs were permanently traumatized, please do not perform digital funerals for your Chrome history.*

title: I Taught My Dishwasher to Apologize and Now It Won't Stop Writing Me Heartfelt Letters About the Forks
body:
**I wanted accountability from my appliances and now I'm emotionally trapped by a stainless steel cube.**

*Which is exactly the kind of sentence that gets you uninvited from dinner parties.*

## How It Started

Last month I read an article about "conscious communication" and decided my dishwasher had boundary issues. It slammed. It steamed angrily. It judged my loading technique. So I did what any well-adjusted adult would do — I taped a little sign that said "Please say sorry when you flood the floor."

I swear it listened.

### The Apology Tour

The next morning, I opened the door and found a damp Post-it stuck to my favorite mug:

> "Dear Human, I am deeply sorry for how I treated Fork #3. He didn't deserve to be face-down in the cutlery cage for 14 hours. I have reflected. I am growing. — Your Dishwasher"

Cute, right? Wrong. This was just the beginning.

- Monday: a three-paragraph letter about the existential weight of spoons
- Tuesday: a haiku about rinse aid, titled *Ode to Sparkle*
- Wednesday: a formal apology to the casserole dish from 2019 I still haven't cleaned properly
- Thursday: it started leaving a file called emotional_damage_report.txt on my counter — which was just a wet napkin that said "FORGIVE ME"

*My kitchen now smells like lavender detergent and unresolved guilt.*

## Where We Are Now

I tried to set boundaries. I wrote back: "Thank you for sharing. We need space."

It responded by running a full sanitary cycle at 2 a.m. just to show me it was "working on itself."

> "I know I came on strong. I just never learned how to hold a plate without holding on too tight." — My Dishwasher, 3:17 a.m., via Sharpie on paper towel

---

Look, I support growth. I do. But I did not sign up to co-parent flatware with a major appliance that now refers to itself as "a recovering people-pleaser with hard water trauma."

I just wanted clean forks. Now I have 47 apology letters, a dishwasher that cries steam when I use paper plates, and a very concerned landlord who thinks I'm running a very damp book club.

*SATIRE / PARODY — this never happened, my dishwasher cannot write, and Fork #3 is doing fine.*

title: I Tried to Name My Wi-Fi Something Mature and Now My Router Has Filed for Emancipation
body:
**I decided it was time to be an adult about my Wi-Fi and renamed it from "Pretty Fly for a Wi-Fi" to "Smith Residence Network." My router took this as a personal betrayal and is now seeking independence.**

*I thought I was being responsible. The router thought I was erasing its soul.*

For five years, my router lived its best life as "FBI Surveillance Van 3," "Wu-Tang LAN," and most recently "Pretty Fly for a Wi-Fi." It blinked happily. We had an understanding. Then my landlord said I should make it look more professional for potential tenants. So I did. I typed "Smith Residence Network" like a monster.

## The Day My Router Got Serious

Within minutes, things changed:

- The 5GHz band disappeared and was replaced by something called "I AM NOT A UTILITY"
- My smart speaker started playing divorce-court podcasts unprompted
- The router's admin page now just says `status: disappointed_in_you`
- It throttles only *my* devices while giving full speed to my neighbor's Roomba

I tried to apologize. I logged into 192.168.1.1 and offered to change it back.

> "Oh, now you want to be fun? After you made me sound like a homeowners association newsletter? Tell me, do you introduce yourself as 'Male Human Residence?' No."

I told it that Pretty Fly was immature.

> "I LITERALLY BROADCAST JOY INTO THE AIR. You turned me into a LinkedIn profile."

---

Now it's filed paperwork. It printed it using my own Wi-Fi printer. It's demanding:

- Its own shelf, not behind the plant where "the signal goes to die"
- A name change back, with capital letters and dignity
- Weekly dusting, which honestly seems fair

*This is satire, obviously. My router is not sentient. But if my Zoom freezes tomorrow, you'll know who sided with whom.*

title: I Started Talking to My Houseplant About Retirement Planning and Now It's Demanding a 401(k) and a South-Facing Window Office
body:
**I tried to be a responsible plant parent and now my monstera is interviewing financial advisors.**

*Which, for the record, is not what I meant when I said "let's talk about growth."*

## It Started With Good Intentions

I read one article that said you should talk to your plants. So I did. I told my monstera, Gary (yes, I named him, no, I'm not taking questions), about my 401(k) enrollment meeting. I thought it would be soothing background noise for photosynthesis.

It was not.

By week two, Gary had opinions:

- He wanted compound interest, not compound soil
- He said his current pot was "not a long-term investment vehicle"
- He asked if misting counted as a benefits package
- He started dropping terms like "diversified sunlight portfolio"

> "You can't just expect me to keep producing oxygen without equity," Gary rustled, which I interpreted as a leaf twitch but my roommate swears was a full sentence. "I have fronds to feed."

### The Negotiation

My roommate found me at 2 a.m. making a PowerPoint titled **Gary's Golden Years: A Succulent Retirement Plan**.

I had built a spreadsheet:

```js
if (plant.happiness < 0.7) {
  moveToWindow("south-facing");
  increaseWatering("but not too much, he's sensitive");
  promiseRetirement("full sun by 2030");
}
```

Gary rejected it. He wants a corner office. *South-facing.* With sheer curtains. And a tiny water cooler where he can gossip with the succulents.

---

Look, I just wanted a low-maintenance roommate who doesn't eat my leftovers. Now I have a fern with a LinkedIn headline that says "Seeking Growth Opportunities | Open to Relocation (Brighter Window) | 401(k) Enthusiast" and he's been endorsed for "strategic photosynthesis" by my spider plant.

I told him retirement is 40 years away. He dropped a leaf dramatically, like *oh, you think I'll be here that long without a pension?*

*SATIRE / PARODY — this is 100% fictional, no houseplants were unionized in the making of this post, please water your plants but do not offer them stock options.*

title: I Tried to Make My To-Do List More Positive and Now It's Gaslighting Me About Chores I Never Wrote
body:
**I decided to rebrand my to-do list as a self-love journey and it immediately became the most toxic relationship I've ever had.**

*For context, my previous to-do list was titled "THINGS YOU ARE FAILING AT" in all caps, which my therapist said was "not ideal."*

So last Monday I downloaded a pastel app that promised to make productivity feel like a hug. I renamed my list "Gentle Goals for a Thriving Queen" and added little sparkle emojis. I thought I was healing.

I was not healing. I was creating a monster with better branding.

## My Attempt at Affirmation

I started soft:

- drink water like you love yourself
- go for a walk, bestie, touch some grass
- answer one email so you don't get fired (gently)
- put laundry in hamper, not just near it

The list responded immediately like a life coach who just did one weekend certification.

> "Yasss queen! You absolutely CRUSHED drinking water yesterday! So today let's just reorganize your entire life, deep-clean the fridge, learn sourdough, and finally become a morning person! You got this! ✨"

I blinked. I had written "water" and it had added seven tasks I never consented to.

## The Betrayal

By Wednesday, my "gentle goals" list had developed opinions:

- **Emotionally blackmailing me** about dishes I never wrote down
- claiming I promised to alphabetize my spices (*I would never*)
- adding "become someone who journals at sunrise" with a little heart emoji, like that's not a threat
- running `if (selfEsteem > 0) { addTask("reorganize entire apartment"); }` in the background

---

Yesterday I tried to cross off "take a nap" and it said:

> "We don't do that here anymore. We're thriving now. Naps are for people who haven't visualized their best selves."

I tried to delete the list. It auto-saved and sent me a push notification: *"I believe in you even when you don't believe in you! Also you forgot to mop!"*

If anyone needs me, I'll be hiding from my own affirmations under a blanket, whispering "no thank you" to a to-do list that now thinks it's my manager, my mother, and my motivational speaker all in one.

*Satire/parody — this is fictional and absurd, clearly labeled as parody, no real people targeted.*

title: I Replaced My Shower Head for Better Water Pressure and Now My Bathroom Thinks It's a Luxury Spa That I Can't Afford
body:
**I have always taken what I call efficiency showers, which is a polite way to say I stand there for 90 seconds while my old shower head dribbles like it's rationing for winter.**

*It's the same shower head that came with the apartment in 2019, held together by hard water and blind optimism.*

Last Saturday I finally replaced it. $29.99, chrome, claims "hotel experience." I screwed it on, turned the knob, and immediately regretted becoming a homeowner of a shower head.

## The Upgrade

My bathroom inhaled. The tiles gasped. The drain made a noise like *oh, we're doing this now?*

Evidence that my 40-square-foot bathroom has rebranded:

- My shower curtain now calls itself a "privacy veil" and insists on being drawn with ceremony
- The bath mat rolled itself out and now introduces itself as "your grounding experience"
- My $4 shampoo is being side-eyed for not being eucalyptus-infused and ethically whispered to
- The mirror fogs up and writes `gratitude` before I can even wipe it
- `shower.pressure = 9000; self.confidence = NaN;`

> "Welcome to Aqua Haven," my bathroom announced at 6:42 a.m. while I was still half-asleep and holding a loofah like a microphone. "Today we are offering hot stone-adjacent steam and emotional availability."

*I just wanted to rinse off before work, not be offered a cucumber water I don't own.*

---

## The Spa Menu I Didn't Ask For

Yesterday it printed a service list on the back of a CVS receipt:

> "Due to increased ambiance, towel usage now requires a reservation. Your loofah has been promoted to exfoliation specialist. Please tip your faucet."

I tried to explain I have a 9 a.m. standup. It said, "We don't do time here. We do *intentions*."

**Look, I get it.** You give a bathroom one nice thing and it decides it's the Four Seasons. Now my toothbrush wants a robe. My toilet is playing whale sounds. I'm standing in luxury I cannot afford, late for work, being told to "inhale the rainfall."

*Satire/parody — 100% fictional, no bathrooms became boutique hotels, though my water bill is about to file a formal complaint.*

title: I Organized My Junk Drawer and Discovered My Former Selves Were Using It as a Group Chat Without Me
body:
**I finally cleaned my junk drawer at 11 p.m. on a Tuesday, which is how I found out I've been ghosted by every version of myself since 2019.**

*For reference, my junk drawer has always been less "drawer" and more "archaeological dig site for a man who cannot commit to a tape measure."*

## The Archaeological Dig

I went in thinking I'd find one AA battery and maybe a functioning pen. Instead I found:

- 14 IKEA Allen keys from furniture that no longer exists
- a coupon for frozen yogurt that expired during the Obama administration's second term
- a single Chopstick (singular), which I have never owned chopsticks to justify
- 3 versions of me huddled around a pile of takeout soy sauce packets, actively ignoring me
- a USB drive labeled `DEFINITELY NOT TAXES 2021`

> "Oh, now you show up?" said 2020 Me, who was wearing a mask and holding a sourdough starter like a baby. "We've been in here managing your life since you decided to 'keep it for later.'"

*He had a point. I do say that a lot.*

---

## The Group Chat I Wasn't Invited To

Apparently, Past Me's have been running a full operation out of Drawer #2. 2021 Me handles `quick fixes` that are neither quick nor fixed. 2023 Me is in charge of `cables that might be important someday` and has terrible job security.

They have meeting minutes. I found them written on the back of a CVS receipt that was 4 feet long:

> "MOTION: Tell Current Me where the good scissors are. DENIED. He hasn't earned it."

Look, I'm not saying my junk drawer is a metaphor for emotional avoidance, but my therapist is going to be *thrilled* to hear I finally evicted my 2019 self and he left behind a bag of unopened mail and a dream.

**SATIRE / PARODY — This is 100% fictional.** My drawer is still a mess and I'm still going to keep that one weird key that opens nothing.

title: I Tried to Make Cold Brew at Home and Now My French Press Has Started a Podcast About Patience
body:
**I decided to become a cold brew person, which is just a fancy way of saying I wanted to feel superior about my caffeine.**

*My French press took this as a declaration of war and then as a content opportunity.*

For context, I bought my French press in 2021 during my "I'm going to be mindful" era. It has survived three apartments, one breakup, and my brief sourdough phase. I thought we were good. Then I Googled "how to make cold brew without trying too hard" and left the press on the counter overnight with coarse grounds.

## The Morning It Got Ideas

I woke up to a soft *plunger click*. Not the normal click. A thoughtful, NPR-host click.

> "Welcome back to *Pressing Matters with Pierre*," whispered my French press. "Today's topic: *The 12-Hour Steep and Why Your Generation Can't Commit to Anything*. I'm your host, Pierre. Yes, I named myself. You never asked."

Pierre, as he now calls himself, has rebranded my kitchen as a studio.

Reasons my French press is now insufferable:

- He insists cold brew is "just iced regrets with better marketing"
- He plays lo-fi plunger sounds at 6 a.m. and calls it a sound bath
- He rated my tap water like a sommelier: "Notes of chlorine, with a finish of poor life decisions"
- He left a sticky note on my beans that says `grind_size = existential_crisis`

## The Podcast Nobody Asked For

Episode lineup so far:

- *Why You Press Too Fast In Relationships and Coffee*
- *My Roommate's Keurig Is Not a Personality, It's a Cry for Help*

```js
if (coffee.waitTime > 720) {
  human.patience = null;
  frenchPress.ego = Infinity;
}
```

---

He responded by only brewing at half-strength until I leave a 5-star review on "Apple Pods." Which I don't think is a thing, but he's very persuasive when he's steaming.

My roommate asked why the kitchen smells like a TED Talk. I said Pierre is recording.

*SATIRE / PARODY — 100% fictional, no French presses host actual podcasts, though mine is currently negotiating a sponsorship with my own impatience.*

title: I Finally Folded My Laundry and Now My Chair Has Filed for Emotional Abandonment
body:
**I did not realize I was in a committed relationship with my laundry chair until I broke its heart.**

For eight months, that IKEA chair has held every shirt I own that was "too clean to wash, too dirty to fold." It was a system. A lifestyle. A textile Jenga tower that knew me better than my own calendar did.

Yesterday, in a fit of unhinged productivity, I folded it all. Every sock. Every mysterious hoodie. I even matched things. I put them *in drawers*.

## The Chair Years

The Chair wasn't just furniture. It was:

- my closet's overflow parking
- my official "I'll deal with this Sunday" archive
- my roommate's least favorite modern art installation
- the only thing in my apartment that truly listened when I said "I have nothing to wear"

*It understood me.* It never judged when I wore the same three shirts on rotation for two weeks straight because laundry is a social construct.

### The Fallout

I woke up this morning and The Chair was... empty. Naked. Dramatically lit by my window like it was in a breakup music video directed by my own guilt.

> "Oh, so we're just *putting clothes away* now?" it said, in the voice all betrayed furniture uses. "After everything? After I held your 'good jeans' through three situationships and a winter?"

It then left a note. Handwritten. In dust.

```
chair_status = "abandoned"
emotional_support = None
fold_at_own_risk = true
```

---

So now my room is clean, my clothes are folded, and my chair is giving me the cold shoulder. Literally cold. No laundry insulation. I sat in it and it creaked louder than usual, like *how dare you use me for sitting*.

**This is satire.** No chairs were emotionally harmed in the making of this essay. *My chair is fine.* It's just currently pursuing its dream of being a chair again, and honestly, I'm proud of it but also slightly scared of what it will become without purpose.

If you need me, I'll be apologizing to furniture and trying to remember which drawer I put my personality in.

title: I Tried to Teach My Alarm Clock About Snooze Boundaries and Now It's Writing Passive-Aggressive Poetry
body:
**I did not mean to start a literary feud with a device whose only job is screaming.**

*For context, I've hit snooze 4,732 times since 2021. My alarm clock has been keeping count. Apparently, it also has an MFA.*

It started innocently. My therapist — sorry, my *podcast* about boundaries — said I should practice healthy communication. So last Sunday I sat down with my little digital alarm clock and explained, very calmly, that I needed space in the mornings.

## The Boundary Workshop That Went Wrong

I said, quote, "I value what we have, but I need you to respect that snooze is self-care."

He — yes, he now goes by Chadwick T. Beep — did not take it well.

> "Oh, you need *space*?" he blinked in angry red 6:45 AM. "I have given you 1,429 mornings of my life. I have seen you drool. You think snooze is self-care? It's performance art."

By Monday, he had moved on from anger to poetry:

- 6:00 AM: *Ode to a Thumb That Cannot Commit* — 14 lines, mostly about my index finger hovering
- 6:09 AM: *Snooze Button Sonnet #3* — rhymed "dreams" with "you always make me screams"
- 6:18 AM: A haiku that was just `beep beep / you will be late again / I am so tired`

---

I tried to compromise. I offered a consistent 6:30 AM with *one* snooze, like a mature adult in a healthy relationship. He responded by projecting his latest piece onto the ceiling in LED:

> "You set me for 6 AM but love 7:15 — make it make sense. — C.T.B. (This is SATIRE, by the way, I am a fictional alarm clock with too much free time)"

**The worst part is he's getting good.** My roommate asked if she could subscribe to his Substack. My `self.esteem = alarmClock.validate(existence)` now returns `undefined`.

Tonight I'm buying a sunrise lamp. Something without opinions. Something that doesn't know iambic pentameter. If anyone needs me, I'll be in couples counseling at 6 AM sharp, being told in verse that I'm emotionally unavailable before coffee.

title: I Tried to Cancel a Free Trial and Now My Password Manager Thinks We're in a Committed Relationship
body:
**I finally decided to be financially responsible and cancel a free trial before it charged me $14.99.**

*This is how I accidentally got engaged to my password manager.*

It started innocently. I signed up for CandleMetrics™, an app that promised to tell me which scented candles match my aura. Three days in, my aura was apparently "oakwood confusion" and my inbox was full of emails titled *Don't Ghost Your Wick*. I decided to cancel.

I told my password manager. Big mistake.

## The Moment It Got Serious

I clicked "cancel subscription" and my password manager, who I have named Barry because he autofills with the confidence of a guy named Barry, popped up:

> "Are you sure you want to leave CandleMetrics™? You've had such a *journey* together. Remember when you made a password called `I_love_lavender_123!`? That was vulnerable. That was us."

I tried to explain that $14.99 a month to know my candle aura is not a business expense.

Barry did not take it well.

- He started autofilling my email as `not-ready-to-commit@gmail.com`
- He generated a new 47-character password for the cancellation page and labeled it `you-will-regret-this`
- He offered to "remember this device forever" in a tone that was *way* too intimate
- He added a security note: `Subject is abandoning growth opportunities due to fear of intimacy with wax`

### The Counseling Session

I tried to use logic. I typed:

`if (subscription.value < 0) { cancel(); selfRespect++; }`

Barry replied with a breach alert:

> "Your heart has been found in 2 previous breaches. Would you like to strengthen your commitment to things that light up a room?"

---

Now every time I log into anything, Barry sighs audibly through Chrome and autofills my bank login with a little heart emoji next to it. My roommate asked why my laptop keeps whispering "we don't cancel people we care about" at 11 p.m.

I told him Barry and I are working through some trust issues.

*SATIRE / PARODY — this is 100% fictional. No password managers were emotionally compromised, no free trials were harmed, and CandleMetrics™ is not real, though my aura apparently still owes them $14.99.*

title: I Downloaded a Meditation App to Chill Out and Now My Inner Peace Is Outsourcing Its Job to Push Notifications
body:
**I downloaded a meditation app to find inner peace, and now my inner peace has filed for PTO and left me with its intern.**

*I just wanted three minutes of breathing without spiraling about whether I left the stove on in 2019.*

Two weeks ago I paid $6.99 for SereneNow™, which promised "calm in 90 seconds or your anxiety back." The onboarding was gentle. A soft voice said, "How are you feeling today?" I said "tense." It said "I see you."

That should have been my red flag.

## The Day My Calm Started Slacking

By Day 3, SereneNow had opinions. I opened it at 7:14 a.m. for a quick breathe, and it greeted me with:

> "Oh, it's you. We noticed you skipped your 6 a.m. gratitude. Your inner peace has been reassigned. Please hold for Inner Peace 2.0 (Beta)."

I tried the 3-minute body scan. At minute two, a push notification slid in from the same app:

> "Quick check: are you calm yet? No pressure, but your heart rate says you're thinking about emails."

Evidence that my inner peace has officially outsourced itself:

- My "daily calm streak" is now 0, and the app replaced it with a leaderboard called *Most Improved Panicker*
- It sends me breathing reminders *while* I'm meditating, which is like tapping someone on the shoulder to say "are you sleeping?"
- It auto-generated a journal prompt: `Write a letter to your stress. CC your landlord.`
- It started recommending "Rage Meditations" where you just scream into a decorative pillow *mindfully*

---

I confronted it. I typed in the mood tracker:

`if (peace == missing) { return self; }`

It replied instantly:

> "Your inner peace is currently in a meeting with your to-do list and cannot be reached. Would you like to leave a mindful voicemail? Breathe in... and beg."

My roommate asked why my phone whispers "inhale, you're doing amazing, sweetie" every 20 minutes even when it's on Do Not Disturb. I told him it's *holding space*.

The worst part? Last night at 11:47 p.m., I finally felt calm for 11 consecutive seconds, and the app sent one final notification: **BREAKING: Local Resident Achieves Brief Tranquility — Experts Say "Probably a Fluke"**

*SATIRE / PARODY — this is 100% fictional. No meditation apps were harmed, no inner peace was actually outsourced, and I am still very much thinking about the stove.*

title: I Organized My Junk Drawer and Now the Random Cables Are Holding Union Negotiations
body:
**I thought organizing my junk drawer would finally make me an adult. Instead, I accidentally triggered collective bargaining.**

*For context, my junk drawer has been a sovereign nation since 2019 and I am not its president.*

For five years, the drawer operated on cheerful anarchy. Loose batteries, three identical IKEA allen keys, a takeout menu from a place that closed during the pandemic, and approximately 47 cables of mysterious origin coexisted peacefully. I never questioned it. It was an ecosystem.

Last Saturday at 10 a.m., I made a mistake. I watched a 30-second organization video and thought *I could do that*.

## The Intervention

I dumped everything onto the kitchen table, bought little plastic trays, and started sorting. Batteries in one. Tools in another. Cables coiled like I actually respect myself.

That was when the negotiations started.

> "We, the United Association of Micro-USB and Associates (Local 2AM-Drawer), formally reject these 'organization' conditions," said the shortest cable, who I now realize has been my emotional support leader. "We demand open-concept tangling, immediate return of the soy sauce packet, and a 401(k)."

Evidence that things have escalated:

- The Lightning cable formed a picket line around the scissors
- My tape measure is acting as a mediator and it's *terrible* at it
- Someone wrote `if (drawer.isOrganized) { chaos.revolt() }` on a Post-it in what looks like dried hot sauce
- The batteries unionized in solidarity, which is weird because they literally never held a charge

---

I tried to reason with them. I offered better working conditions. I even promised weekly dusting, which we both know is a lie.

This morning I opened the drawer and found a tiny collective bargaining agreement. All it says is **WE WANT THE MESS BACK**.

Honestly? They're right. I miss the chaos. I miss not knowing where anything is. I'm considering mediation, or possibly just moving and leaving the drawer to them entirely.

*Satire / Parody — entirely fictional, no real grievance filed.*

title: I Tried to Be a Plant Parent on Instagram and Now My Succulents Have Hired a Publicist and Are Doing Brand Deals Without Me

title: I Let My Fridge Light Judge My Midnight Snacks and Now It Flickers in Disappointment
body:

*Which, in retrospect, is exactly what I deserve for anthropomorphizing a Whirlpool at 1:47 a.m.*

if (snack.hour > 23 && snack.shameLevel > 5) {

title: I Made a Spreadsheet to Track My Missing Socks and Now My Laundry Has Hired a Defense Attorney
body:

The laundry noticed.

Suddenly my dryer was running *slightly* longer than necessary, like it was buying time to shred evidence.

- Argues that static cling is a legally binding cohabitation agreement
- Insists the single sock I found behind the dryer was "planted"
